thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: pagerduty -> #incidents: Multiple node provisioning failures detected across eu-west-1 during autoscale. alert_id=PD12345

jamie: seeing tons of new nodes stuck in ContainerCreating, kubelet logs show repeated 401/429 from registry during manifest fetch. autoscaler is spinning up but pods never start.

maria: confirmed. failures correlated to `nvcr.io` and `auth.docker.io` errors. sample from kubelet: `manifest request GET https://nvcr.io/v2/nvidia/cuda/manifests/11.8: 401 Unauthorized` then `auth.docker.io token exchange 429`.

ben: copying useful logs to thread.

ben: kubectl describe pod nginx-xxx -> "Failed to pull image \"nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda:11.8\": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to pull and unpack image: failed to resolve reference: unexpected status code [manifests 401]"

alex: noticed a surge in provisioning since 02:03 UTC (traffic spike). cloud autoscaler requested ~200 nodes; first 120 got images, then registry started rejecting with 429. might be rate limit on auth token service or a signing service outage.

jamie: initial mitigation plan: 1) pause autoscaling (scale down requests), 2) enable fallback to AMI baked images (pre-pulled) for critical pools, 3) flip to internal registry mirror for non-Dedicated infra. I'll start on 1 and 2.

maria: opening vendor ticket with NVIDIA/Docker auth team, link to status: https://status.docker.com and https://status.nvidia.com — latter currently has no incident. sending logs and timestamps.

pagerduty: PagerDuty alert acknowledged by jamie.

ben: jamie: when you pause autoscaler, can you also set cluster-autoscaler to prefer nodes with pre-pulled AMI label? we have a small pool with prewarmed images.

jamie: yes doing: `kubectl annotate nodepool prewarmed=true` + patch CA config to prefer. putting cluster-autoscaler into "scale-down disabled" mode temporarily.

alex: started deploying a daemonset to pre-pull critical images from our internal mirror (artifacts.internal.redwood). it's rolling; should help for later nodes.

maria: vendor responded: "We are investigating increased rate limiting on token service affecting manifest requests for some namespaces; engineering engaged." they asked for client request IDs. gave them example headers and timestamps.

ben: for immediate customer-facing mitigation we should: - mark Dedicated provisioning as degraded in status page - divert new Dedicated requests to hosted pools in other regions - increase imagePull backoff to reduce repeated failed pulls

jamie: updating status page now: "Provisioning degraded in eu-west-1: experiencing image registry auth failures causing delayed node provisioning." :warning:

maria: also notifying support to flag impacted customers who recently created Dedicated nodes. sending list of recent requests.

ben: added a short-lived workaround: update kubelet config via kubelet-config ConfigMap to add `--image-pull-progress-deadline=10m` and bump `imagePullBackoff` retry window. this reduces tight retry loops hitting the auth service repeatedly.

alex: cloud provider (GCP) ticket opened in parallel — they confirmed no network issues on our VPC. suggests upstream registry token service is the culprit.

jamie: handoff to ben for overnight. jamie -> ben: summary pinned. actions done: autoscaler paused, prewarmed pool annotated, daemonset deploy started, status page updated, vendor ticket opened.

ben: taking over. I'm going to run a quick sweep to ensure no pods in Pending for >20m that aren't covered by prewarmed pool. will also temporarily set a rate-limit-friendly backoff policy in the image pull controller.

maria: vendor update: "We've mitigated a token service overload by increasing capacity. You may still see 401/429 for up to 10 minutes due to caches. If you continue to see 401s after 10 minutes, please provide sample request-ids."

ben: I'm seeing a gradual drop in new failures since +8m. nodes that used the mirror are booting fine. a handful of customers still seeing provisioning failures — support notified and we have an inbound support ticket flow.

jamie: quick note — we should consider baking critical images into AMIs in all regions to avoid future manifest auth dependency during initial node join. adding to action items.

maria: vendor now reports suppression of the surge. they recommend implementing token cache/retry jitter on client side. also suggested using short-lived auth tokens but with exponential backoff.

ben: marking incident as mitigated for now. leaving autoscaler paused until we confirm no new 401/429s for 30m. will re-enable with aggressive backoff and prefer prewarmed nodes.

jamie: postmortem TODOs that I recorded in thread — add runbook: - bake pre-pulled AMI images for critical CUDA tags - add registry health probe and page on increased 401/429 rate - autoscaler could fall back to prewarmed pools on registry failures - ensure support runbook for customer notification templates

alex: we'll also add a daemon that mirrors critical nvcr images to artifacts.internal.redwood on publish. ops ticket created: OPS-897.

maria: closing vendor ticket with logs attached. will follow up if we see regression.

ben: leaving detailed handover notes in oncall doc and scheduling a quick sync at 14:00 UTC to run through follow-ups. great work everyone. :thumbsup:

jamie: thanks — continuing to monitor. please escalate if anything else pops up.

incident-bot: Incident closed (mitigated) by ben at 1813457099.
